detail: finding: Despite the portal and the plan for 171 services, people and businesses still lack real e-services and face fragmented administration.
intervention: The e-Government portal launched in December 2024; the first e-services were integrated in April of the year of the event.
outcome: The portal improved information: citizens can now see the responsible institution, the cost and the documents and forms required.
finding: A ministry official says citizens want the government portal as a single entry point, not many websites.
barrier: A UNDP speaker says the real issue is the lack of e-services, not fear of technology.
recommendation: Data should be in multiple formats, signatures and payments should underpin e-services, and the portal should be the central hub.
finding: Citizens have to contact institutions individually, which wastes time.
finding: After three years, the same problems persist.
